title: Add VPC control plane Terraform: multi-AZ interface endpoints, SG peering, Route53 delegation
author: Priya Kaur
body:
Motivation: Private control plane VPC provisioning needs multi-AZ resilience and tighter network controls for enterprise customers. This PR extends the Terraform module used by the private-installer to add: 1) Multi-AZ subnet provisioning for control-plane nodes, 2) configurable interface (AWS) endpoints for S3, ECR and STS to support air-gapped/private deployments, 3) security group topology and cross-account peering/security group rules to support dedicated control-plane peering from customer app VPCs, and 4) Route53 delegated hosted zone support for cross-account DNS delegation + optional resolver rules. The changes are intended to provide repeatable, auditable infra for private deployments and to standardize network patterns across regions.

What this PR changes: - New module: modules/vpc-control-plane/multi_az.tf (creates subnets, route tables, AZ-aware tagging) - New module: modules/vpc-control-plane/interface_endpoints.tf (creates aws_vpc_endpoint and aws_vpc_endpoint_service or private_interface_endpoints as appropriate, with security group attachment) - Security groups: modules/vpc-control-plane/sg.tf (strict least-priv SGs, egress-only for secrets endpoints, explicit peering rules) - Peering & routing: modules/vpc-control-plane/peering.tf (cross-account VPC peering, route propagation, validation outputs) - DNS: modules/vpc-control-plane/route53.tf (delegation role/policy, optional Route53 resolver rules) - Variables + examples: modules/vpc-control-plane/variables.tf, examples/multi-az-control-plane/README.md - Upgrade hooks: templates/upgrade-hooks/README.md and scripts/rollback-check.sh to validate peering and resolver state before rolling upgrades.

Backward compatibility: All new modules are opt-in via a top-level bool var enable_control_plane_vpc. Existing behavior is preserved when false. The module exposes outputs (control_plane_vpc_id, az_subnet_ids, endpoint_ids, delegation_role_arn) to wire into the installer. We avoided changing existing resource names to prevent accidental replacement.

Testing & verification: - Unit Terraform: terraform fmt/validate and plan runs added to CI for the module. - Integration: deployed to dev account (us-west-2) with multi-AZ enabled; verified control plane nodes provision and can reach S3/ECR via interface endpoints. - Peering: validated cross-account peering with staging app VPC (route propagation and SG rules working). - DNS: tested Route53 delegation to customer account and resolver rules for internal domains. See CI logs and integration plan output for details.

Rollout plan: 1) Merge to main behind feature flag (enable_control_plane_vpc=false by default). 2) Incremental rollout via private-installer CI: enable in a single dev region and validate. 3) Enable for customer onboarding after manual verification. Rollback: set enable_control_plane_vpc=false and run terraform apply in control-plane workspace; scripts/rollback-check.sh ensures peering/route cleanup before destroying resources.

Checklist: - [x] Terraform module + examples added - [x] Unit/format validation in CI - [x] Integration in dev account - [x] Docs example and README - [x] Rollback script included

Related: ENG-4567 (design doc), INFRA-129 (peering requirements), SUP-789 (customer request).
commits: initial: add multi-az subnet and route table logic
add interface endpoints and secgroup attachments
add peering and route propagation boilerplate
tests: add terraform validate/plan CI jobs
chore: fix naming collisions and add unit tests
review_comments: Daniel Kim: Can we avoid creating interface endpoints in accounts that already have centralized endpoints? Suggest adding a var to opt-out per service.
Priya Kaur: Good catch — added per-service enable flags and a list var to skip services. Also added a validation rule to fail if all services are skipped.
Maya Chen: Need clearer IAM boundary for the delegation role; can we scope it down and add an expiration/rotation note?
Priya Kaur: Scoped the delegation role to a tight policy (Route53:ChangeResourceRecordSets on the delegated subdomain only) and documented rotation steps in examples.
Liam O'Connor: CI plan looks good, but the peering logic should check for overlapping CIDR ranges before creating peering connections.
Priya Kaur: Added preflight CIDR-overlap check in scripts/rollback-check.sh and terraform validation (terraform local-exec guard).
merge_commit: squash! add vpc control plane multi-az endpoints and peering (431789)
release_notes: Added opt-in Terraform modules to provision multi-AZ control plane VPCs with interface endpoints, security groups, cross-account peering, and Route53 delegation. Modules are opt-in; see examples/multi-az-control-plane/README.md for upgrade and rollback steps.
notes_for_ops: When enabling for an existing customer, run the integration plan in a staging account first. Ensure peering CIDRs do not overlap; validate Route53 delegation with the customer account before enabling. Use scripts/rollback-check.sh to verify safe destroy order.
